title: docs(cli): say what `objectui check` does; point to `objectui validate` for the verdict
body:
Fixes #10416
Clause-②: no

Docs only. Two published pages promised a validation verdict that `objectui check` does not give. They now say what `check` does and send the reader to `objectui validate` for the verdict. `check` itself is unchanged. objectui#6318 recorded its behaviour as deliberate, and whether `check` should parse the files it admits is the product decision that record left open. It is not part of this card.

## What changed

- `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md`, section "Render is not a validation door":
  - Door 2 is now `objectui validate`. It parses one document (JSON or YAML) against the published schema, prints the schema's own errors and exits non-zero.
  - The `check` sentence now describes what `check` does. It sweeps JSON files and recognises a file by a root structural key (`children`, `className`, `body`, …) without parsing it. Only a file with none of those keys is parsed. A file with a registered `type` that fails that parse is listed as an advisory, and `check` exits non-zero on unreadable JSON only. The sentence links to the `objectui check` section of the CLI reference.
  - Door 3 now calls `safeValidateSchema` "the parse `objectui validate` runs". It used to say "the same parse both CLI commands run".
- `content/docs/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`, the `requestBody` row: the refusal of the retired `body` key comes from `objectui validate` or the type checker. The row now says `check` does not deliver it. `body` is itself a structural key, so `check` never parses a file that has `body` at its root.

## Measurement, taken before the rewrite

The CLI was built from this branch's base `a98335770` with `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/cli...' build`. This PR changes no code, so the binary at the head is the same. I wrote four throwaway documents, and each one fails schema validation:

| file | content | why it is in the set |
|---|---|---|
| `flex-structural.json` | `{ "type": "flex", "direction": "column", "children": [] }` | the objectui#8761 shape: an invalid `direction`, and the root carries `children` |
| `chatbot-body.json` | `{ "type": "chatbot", "messages": [], "body": { "tenant": "acme" } }` | the plugin-chatbot row's own case, the retired `body` key |
| `chatbot-leaf.json` | `{ "type": "chatbot", "messages": "not-an-array" }` | control: the root has no structural key |
| `flex-leaf.yaml` | `type: flex` and `direction: column` | a YAML document |

### `objectui validate FILE`: exit 1 on all four

`flex-structural.json`, exit 1 (`flex-leaf.yaml` gives the same error block, also exit 1):

```
✗ Schema validation failed!

Validation Errors:

1. Invalid option: expected one of "row"|"col"|"row-reverse"|"col-reverse"
   Path: direction
   Code: invalid_value
```

`chatbot-body.json`, exit 1:

```
✗ Schema validation failed!

Validation Errors:

1. REFUSED (objectui#8572, ADR-0049) — `body` is the CONTENT slot on every other component, and `chatbot` reads NEITHER content channel; this arm restated it as the chat API body params, the one place in this vocabulary where the key carried two meanings. Author the chat API params as `requestBody` instead — the key the registration forwards to the chat runtime as its `body` option, and the key the `chatbot-enhanced` and `chatbot-floating` twins already declare. Delete `body` here: nothing renders it, and nothing sends it.
   Path: body
   Code: invalid_type
```

`chatbot-leaf.json`, exit 1:

```
1. Invalid input: expected array, received string
   Path: messages
   Code: invalid_type
```

### `objectui check` in the directory that holds all four: exit 0

```
Object UI Schema Check
Analyzing 4 files...
⚠️ 1 file carries a registered ObjectUI component type but did not validate as an ObjectUI schema:
   chatbot-leaf.json (type "chatbot")
   Run `objectui validate FILE` on any of them for the reason.
   Either the document is off-spec, or its component type is not modelled by @object-ui/types.
   These are NOT counted as skipped: a schema that fails validation is a broken schema, not a foreign file.
✓ All checks passed
```

In this block, `FILE` replaces the angle-bracket placeholder the CLI prints, because GitHub's body sanitizer deletes that shape.

What the two runs show: all four documents fail `validate`. `check` lists one of them, the control with no structural key, then prints `All checks passed` and exits 0. It admits `flex-structural.json` by its `children` key and `chatbot-body.json` by its `body` key, and parses neither of them. It never reads `flex-leaf.yaml`, because only the `.json` branch parses anything. So the card's premise holds on `a98335770`.

## Other places that make the same promise

I searched the whole tree with `git grep -n -i -E 'objectui (check|validate)'`, excluding CHANGELOGs and `.changeset/`, and read every `check` hit in context.

This PR changes only the two pages above. Nothing else in `content/docs/**`, in the package READMEs or in the chatbot plugin's own README makes this promise. Two pages already describe `check` correctly, so they are left as they are:

- `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx`: its `objectui check` section is the one the new wording links to, and it says "Only unreadable JSON makes `objectui check` exit non-zero".
- `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`.

Three more places make the same promise. They are outside this card's file surface, so this PR reports them to the seat and does not change them:

- `skills/objectui/guides/project-setup.md`: the CLI table's `objectui check` row reads "Validate every schema file in the project". `skills/**` is a governed surface, so this needs its own PR.
- `packages/cli/src/cli.ts`: the `--help` description of the `check` command is `Validate schema files`. The card rules out any CLI change.
- `packages/types/src/complex.ts`: the JSDoc on `ChatbotSchema.body` says the refusal comes from "a root parse (`objectui validate` / `objectui check`, which call `safeValidateSchema`)". That is the same sentence the chatbot row carried. It ships in `@object-ui/types` `dist/complex.d.ts`, so changing it changes published source, and a changeset is owed.

## Acceptance notes

These are not filed.

- Two test comments say `check` validates `search-interface.json`: `packages/types/src/__tests__/filter-builder-mirror-6939.test.ts` ("runs `safeValidateSchema` on the ROOT only") and `examples/schema-catalog/test/filter-builder-operator-vocabulary-6939.test.tsx` ("validates the parsed document rather than each child"). That file's root carries `className` and `children`, so `check` never parses it. Neither test's assertions depend on this.
- The JSDoc for the semantic sectioning tags in `packages/types/src/layout.ts` says that, before objectui#8499, a document "was refused by `objectui check`". This describes the past, and in any case `check` never refuses a document for failing validation.
- `check` matches `.yaml` and `.yml` files but never parses them, which its own comment says. The new schema-rendering wording therefore says "a project's JSON files".

## Gates at head `16c22c0c6`

| gate | verdict line it printed | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm check:doc-snippets`, after `turbo run build` of its `--build-filter` closure (35/35 tasks) | `Semantic phase: 673 of 673 block(s) judged, 0 failed.` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:doc-examples` | `Every covered @example compiles, or fails exactly as its ledger row declares.` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-doc-fence-languages.mjs --self-test`, then the same script without the flag | `check:doc-fences — every TypeScript block in 227 document(s) is fenced ts/tsx/typescript …` | 0 and 0 |
| `pnpm docs:check-links` | `Links are valid across 17 scan roots.` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:doc-types` | `Every documented component type is registered.` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:doc-example-ids` | `414 real reference(s) all resolve in the catalog registry.` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | `check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 8585 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:doc-example-readers` and `node scripts/check-prompt-component-keys.mjs` | `OK …` | 0 and 0 |

Tests that read these pages as input: `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --changed` lists both edited paths. I ran `pnpm exec vitest run packages/components/src/__tests__/guide-schema-rendering-data-context-8021.test.tsx packages/types/src/__tests__/chat-message-avatar-keys-7295.test.ts scripts/__tests__/check-doc-component-types.test.ts`. Result: `Test Files 3 passed (3)`, `Tests 157 passed (157)`.

The link checker does judge the new anchor. A one-off mutation proved it. `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` from objectstack changed `/docs/utilities/cli#objectui-check` to `#objectui-chek` (anchor count 1 to 0, blob `372f4035` to `9c5425ff`). `docs:check-links` then exited 1 with an `[anchor]` finding that names `/docs/utilities/cli#objectui-chek`. After the restore, the blob equals HEAD's `372f4035` and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

No changeset is owed: the presence gate's verdict is quoted above.

Written by the dispatched dev for the `domain:ui` seat 1, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`.
